staked_eth_amount.meaning: amount of ETH the user staked, reported as 1 ETH

l1_command_1_queued.meaning: L1 Undelegate Command #1 was added to the L1 operations queue by the user's withdrawal request

withdrawal_cancelled_before_processing.meaning: the withdrawal was cancelled before pending withdrawals were processed via processL1Withdrawals

l1_command_1_still_queued.meaning: L1 Command #1 remains in the L1 operations queue after the L2 cancellation

l2_l1_state_desynced.meaning: L2 state and L1 state are desynchronized, i.e. the L2 cancellation is not reflected in the L1 operations queue

assumptions: The cancellation is performed by the StakingManager on L2 and only updates L2 state, as described in the root-cause statements.
The L1 operations queue is processed by the operator via processL1Operations after the cancellation.
The user re-queues a withdrawal using the same kHYPE returned from the cancellation, adding L1 Command #2.

unresolved.description: Report does not state who cancels the withdrawal or what triggers cancellation; the cancellation actor/trigger is unspecified.
Report does not state whether the user is authorized or whether anyone can call the relevant functions.

limitations: The selected impact l1_l2_desync is formalized as the absence of L2/L1 state desynchronization after a cancelled withdrawal whose L1 command remains queued; the 2 ETH vs 1 ETH double-withdrawal magnitude is not part of this impact's predicate.
The desynchronization is represented as a grounded Boolean because the report states the condition qualitatively without a numeric definition of the L2/L1 state correspondence.
The cancellation trigger and authorization scope are not specified in the report and are left as nonblocking clarifications.
